slides.headline: He crowned himself. Look who isn't really there.
slides.sub: Jacques-Louis David, The Coronation of Napoleon, 1805-07

slides.headline: Notre-Dame, 1804
slides.text: Paris, 2 December 1804. Inside Notre-Dame, Napoleon becomes Emperor of the French. The Pope himself has come all the way from Rome.

slides.headline: The crown
slides.text: Napoleon took the crown from the Pope's hands and crowned himself. David shows the next moment: now he crowns Josephine.

slides.headline: Josephine
slides.text: Josephine kneels before him, young and radiant. She was older than Napoleon, and gossip said David made her look younger.

slides.headline: The Pope
slides.text: Behind them, Pope Pius VII sits and raises his hand in blessing. Napoleon is said to have asked David to add that gesture.

slides.headline: The mother
slides.text: And in the place of honour sits Napoleon's mother, Letizia. In reality she was not there. She had stayed away from Paris.

slides.headline: The painter
slides.text: Up in the gallery, David painted himself, drawing the scene. He really was there that day, watching every detail.

slides.headline: A giant
slides.text: The canvas is almost ten metres wide, with well over a hundred portraits. It took David nearly three years to finish.

slides.headline: Edited history
slides.text: A real event, edited like propaganda: a mother added, a gesture improved. Would you rewrite your big day to look perfect?
